correctness.rationale: In the exact Hardy H² norm, h(z)=product_(k>=1)(1-q^k z)^(-p) and its inverse are bounded analytic multipliers: h(z)=(1-qz)^(-p)h(qz). Hence T=M_h C_q M_h^(-1), with simple q^n eigenvalues and unit-normalized hz^n/sqrt(N). The extremal multiplier boundary moduli align at z=+1 and z=-1; analytic Fejér-polynomial concentration proves both sharp Riesz constants. Rank-one coefficient projection P_n has norm ||h||_2 (sum_(j<=n)|[z^j](1/h)|²)^(1/2), and Parseval yields its limit. Improper Riemann sums of -log(1-e^-x), log(1+e^-x) and a boundary arc of width epsilon² justify p*pi²/2 versus p*pi²/4 logarithmic growth rates. Critical endpoints 0<q<1 and p>1 retained; the zero spectral point is not misidentified as a nonzero eigenvalue. Finite independent Toeplitz-multiplier calculations at p=2.3,q=.42 found finite-section extreme singular values approaching the stated bounds, but are not a proof.
